verses.zh: 大卫的死期临近了，就嘱咐他儿子所罗门说：
verses.en: When David was close to death,[NOTE:1] he told[NOTE:2] Solomon his son:
notes: Heb “and the days of David approached to die.”
Or “commanded.”

verses.zh: 「我现在要走世人必走的路。所以，你当刚强，作大丈夫，
verses.en: “I am about to die.[NOTE:1] Be strong and become a man!
notes: Heb “going the way of all the earth.”

verses.zh: 遵守耶和华―你　神所吩咐的，照着摩西律法上所写的行主的道，谨守他的律例、诫命、典章、法度。这样，你无论做甚么事，不拘往何处去，尽都亨通。
verses.en: Do the job the Lord your God has assigned you[NOTE:1] by following his instructions[NOTE:2] and obeying[NOTE:3] his rules, commandments, regulations, and laws as written in the law of Moses. Then you will succeed in all you do and seek to accomplish,[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “keep the charge of the Lord your God.”
Heb “by walking in his ways.”
Or “keeping.”
Heb “then you will cause to succeed all which you do and all which you turn there.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必成就向我所应许的话说：『你的子孙若谨慎自己的行为，尽心尽意诚诚实实地行在我面前，就不断人坐以色列的国位。』
verses.en: and the Lord will fulfill his promise to me,[NOTE:1] ‘If your descendants watch their step[NOTE:2] and live faithfully in my presence[NOTE:3] with all their heart and being,[NOTE:4] then,’ he promised,[NOTE:5] ‘you will not fail to have a successor on the throne of Israel.’[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “then the Lord will establish his word which he spoke to me, saying.”
Heb “guard their way.”
Heb “by walking before me in faithfulness.”
Or “soul.”
Heb “saying.”
Heb “there will not be cut off from you a man from upon the throne of Israel.”

verses.zh: 你知道洗鲁雅的儿子约押向我所行的，就是杀了以色列的两个元帅：尼珥的儿子押尼珥和益帖的儿子亚玛撒。他在太平之时流这二人的血，如在争战之时一样，将这血染了腰间束的带和脚上穿的鞋。
verses.en: “You know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—how he murdered two commanders of the Israelite armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether.[NOTE:1] During peacetime he struck them down as if in battle;[NOTE:2] when he shed their blood, he stained the belt on his waist and the sandals on his feet.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “what he did to the two commanders…and he killed them.”
Heb “he shed the blood of battle in peace.”

Heb “and he shed the blood of battle on his belt which is on his waist and on his sandal[s] which are on his feet.” That is, he covered himself with guilt and his guilt was obvious to all who saw him.

verses.zh: 所以你要照你的智慧行，不容他白头安然下阴间。
verses.en: Do to him what you think is appropriate,[NOTE:1] but don’t let him live long and die a peaceful death.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “according to your wisdom.”
Heb “and do not bring down his grey hair in peace [to] Sheol.”

verses.zh: 你当恩待基列人巴西莱的众子，使他们常与你同席吃饭；因为我躲避你哥哥押沙龙的时候，他们拿食物来迎接我。
verses.en: “Treat fairly[NOTE:1] the sons of Barzillai of Gilead and provide for their needs,[NOTE:2] because they helped me[NOTE:3] when I had to flee from your brother Absalom.
notes: Heb “do loyalty with”; or “act faithfully toward.”
Heb “and let them be among the ones who eat [at] your table.”
Heb “thus drew near to.”

verses.zh: 在你这里有巴户琳的便雅悯人，基拉的儿子示每；我往玛哈念去的那日，他用狠毒的言语咒骂我，后来却下约旦河迎接我，我就指着耶和华向他起誓说：『我必不用刀杀你。』
verses.en: “Note well, you still have to contend with Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim,[NOTE:1] who tried to call down upon me a horrible judgment when I went to Mahanaim.[NOTE:2] He came down and met me at the Jordan, and I solemnly promised[NOTE:3] him by the Lord, ‘I will not strike you down[NOTE:4] with the sword.’
notes: Heb “Look, with you is Shimei….”
Heb “and he cursed me with a horrible curse on the day I went to Mahanaim.”
Or “swore an oath to.”
Heb “kill you.”

verses.zh: 现在你不要以他为无罪。你是聪明人，必知道怎样待他，使他白头见杀，流血下到阴间。」
verses.en: But now[NOTE:1] don’t treat him as if he were innocent. You are a wise man and you know how to handle him;[NOTE:2] make sure he has a bloody death.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The Lucianic recension of the Old Greek and the Vulgate have here “you” rather than “now.” The two words are homonyms in Hebrew.
Heb “what you should do to him.”
Heb “bring his grey hair down in blood [to] Sheol.”

verses.zh: 大卫与他列祖同睡，葬在大卫城。
verses.en: Then David passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried in the City of David.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and David lay down with his fathers.”
The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.

verses.zh: 大卫作以色列王四十年：在希伯仑作王七年，在耶路撒冷作王三十三年。
verses.en: David reigned over Israel forty years; he reigned in Hebron seven years, and in Jerusalem[NOTE:1] thirty-three years.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 所罗门坐他父亲大卫的位，他的国甚是坚固。
verses.en: Solomon sat on his father David’s throne, and his royal authority[NOTE:1] was firmly solidified.
notes: Or “kingship.”

verses.zh: 哈及的儿子亚多尼雅去见所罗门的母亲拔示巴，拔示巴问他说：「你来是为平安吗？」回答说：「是为平安」；
verses.en: Haggith’s son Adonijah visited Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother. She asked, “Do you come in peace?” He answered, “Yes.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[in] peace.”

verses.zh: 又说：「我有话对你说。」拔示巴说：「你说吧。」
verses.en: He added,[NOTE:1] “I have something to say to you.” She replied, “Speak.”
notes: Heb “and he said.”

verses.zh: 亚多尼雅说：「你知道国原是归我的，以色列众人也都仰望我作王，不料，国反归了我兄弟，因他得国是出乎耶和华。
verses.en: He said, “You know that the kingdom[NOTE:1] was mine and all Israel considered me king.[NOTE:2] But then the kingdom was given to my brother, for the Lord decided it should be his.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “kingship.”
Heb “set their face to me to be king.”
Heb “and the kingdom turned about and became my brother’s, for from the Lord it became his.”

verses.zh: 现在我有一件事求你，望你不要推辞。」拔示巴说：「你说吧。」
verses.en: Now I’d like to ask you for just one thing. Please don’t refuse me.”[NOTE:1] She said, “Go ahead and ask.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Do not turn back my face.”
Heb “She said, ‘Speak!’”

verses.zh: 他说：「求你请所罗门王将书念的女子亚比煞赐我为妻，因他必不推辞你。」
verses.en: He said, “Please ask King Solomon if he would give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife, for he won’t refuse you.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Say to Solomon the king, for he will not turn back your face, that he might give to me Abishag the Shunammite for a wife.”

verses.zh: 拔示巴说：「好，我必为你对王提说。」
verses.en: Bathsheba replied, “That’s fine;[NOTE:1] I’ll speak to the king on your behalf.”
notes: Heb “[It is] good!”

verses.zh: 于是，拔示巴去见所罗门王，要为亚多尼雅提说；王起来迎接，向她下拜，就坐在位上，吩咐人为王母设一座位，她便坐在王的右边。
verses.en: So Bathsheba visited King Solomon to speak to him on Adonijah’s behalf. The king got up to greet[NOTE:1] her, bowed to her, and then sat on his throne. He ordered a throne to be brought for the king’s mother,[NOTE:2] and she sat at his right hand.
notes: Or “meet.”
Heb “he set up a throne for the mother of the king.”

verses.zh: 拔示巴说：「我有一件小事求你，望你不要推辞。」王说：「请母亲说，我必不推辞。」
verses.en: She said, “I would like to ask you for just one small favor.[NOTE:1] Please don’t refuse me.”[NOTE:2] He said,[NOTE:3] “Go ahead and ask, my mother, for I would not refuse you.”
notes: Or “I’d like to make just one request of you.”
Heb “Do not turn back my face.”
Heb “and the king said to her.”

verses.zh: 拔示巴说：「求你将书念的女子亚比煞赐给你哥哥亚多尼雅为妻。」
verses.en: She said, “Allow Abishag the Shunammite to be given to your brother Adonijah as a wife.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王对他母亲说：「为何单替他求书念的女子亚比煞呢？也可以为他求国吧！他是我的哥哥，他有祭司亚比亚他和洗鲁雅的儿子约押为辅佐。」
verses.en: King Solomon answered his mother, “Why just request Abishag the Shunammite for him?[NOTE:1] Since he is my older brother, you should also request the kingdom for him, for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”
notes: Heb “for Adonijah.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王就指着耶和华起誓说：「亚多尼雅这话是自己送命，不然，愿　神重重地降罚与我。
verses.en: King Solomon then swore an oath by the Lord, “May God judge me severely,[NOTE:1] if Adonijah does not pay for this request with his life![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “So may God do to me, and so may he add.”
Heb “if with his life Adonijah has not spoken this word.”

verses.zh: 耶和华坚立我，使我坐在父亲大卫的位上，照着所应许的话为我建立家室；现在我指着永生的耶和华起誓，亚多尼雅今日必被治死。」
verses.en: Now, as certainly as the Lord lives (he who made me secure, allowed me to sit on my father David’s throne, and established a dynasty[NOTE:1] for me as he promised), Adonijah will be executed today!”
notes: Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 于是所罗门王差遣耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，将亚多尼雅杀死。
verses.en: King Solomon then sent[NOTE:1] Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he killed Adonijah.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text adds, “by the hand of.”
Heb “and he struck him and he died.”

verses.zh: 王对祭司亚比亚他说：「你回亚拿突归自己的田地去吧！你本是该死的，但因你在我父亲大卫面前抬过主耶和华的约柜，又与我父亲同受一切苦难，所以我今日不将你杀死。」
verses.en: The king then told Abiathar the priest, “Go back to your property[NOTE:1] in Anathoth. You deserve to die,[NOTE:2] but today I will not kill you because you did carry the ark of the Sovereign Lord before my father David and you suffered with my father through all his difficult times.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “field.”
Heb “you are a man of death,” an idiom.
Heb “and because you suffered through all which my father suffered.”

verses.zh: 所罗门就革除亚比亚他，不许他作耶和华的祭司。这样，便应验耶和华在示罗论以利家所说的话。
verses.en: Solomon removed Abiathar from being a priest for the Lord, fulfilling the Lord’s message that he had pronounced against the family of Eli in Shiloh.

verses.zh: 约押虽然没有归从押沙龙，却归从了亚多尼雅。他听见这风声，就逃到耶和华的帐幕，抓住祭坛的角。
verses.en: When the news reached Joab (for Joab had supported[NOTE:1] Adonijah, although he had not supported Absalom), he[NOTE:2] ran to the tent of the Lord and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “turned after” (also later in this verse).
Heb “Joab.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

Grabbed hold of the horns of the altar. The “horns” of the altar were the horn-shaped projections on the four corners of the altar (see Exod 27:2). By going to the holy place and grabbing hold of the horns of the altar, Joab was seeking asylum from Solomon.

verses.zh: 有人告诉所罗门王说：「约押逃到耶和华的帐幕，现今在祭坛的旁边。」所罗门就差遣耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，说：「你去将他杀死。」
verses.en: When King Solomon heard[NOTE:1] that Joab had run to the tent of the Lord and was right there beside the altar, he ordered Benaiah son of Jehoiada,[NOTE:2] “Go, strike him down.”
notes: Heb “and it was related to King Solomon.”
Heb “so Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying.”

verses.zh: 比拿雅来到耶和华的帐幕，对约押说：「王吩咐说，你出来吧！」他说：「我不出去，我要死在这里。」比拿雅就去回覆王，说约押如此如此回答我。
verses.en: When Benaiah arrived at the tent of the Lord, he said to him, “The king says, ‘Come out!’” But he replied, “No, I will die here!” So Benaiah sent word to the king and reported Joab’s reply.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “saying, “In this way Joab spoke and in this way he answered me.”

verses.zh: 王说：「你可以照着他的话行，杀死他，将他葬埋，好叫约押流无辜人血的罪不归我和我的父家了。
verses.en: The king told him, “Do as he said! Strike him down and bury him. Take away from me and from my father’s family[NOTE:1] the guilt of Joab’s murderous, bloody deeds.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “take away the undeserved bloodshed which Joab spilled from upon me and from upon the house of my father.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必使约押流人血的罪归到他自己的头上；因为他用刀杀了两个比他又义又好的人，就是以色列元帅尼珥的儿子押尼珥和犹大元帅益帖的儿子亚玛撒，我父亲大卫却不知道。
verses.en: May the Lord punish him for the blood he shed;[NOTE:1] behind my father David’s back he struck down and murdered with the sword two men who were more innocent and morally upright than he[NOTE:2]—Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.
notes: Heb “The Lord will cause his blood to return upon his head.”
Heb “because he struck down two men more innocent and better than he and he killed them with the sword, and my father David did not know.”

verses.zh: 故此，流这二人血的罪必归到约押和他后裔的头上，直到永远；惟有大卫和他的后裔，并他的家与国，必从耶和华那里得平安，直到永远。」
verses.en: May Joab and his descendants be perpetually guilty of their shed blood, but may the Lord give perpetual peace to David, his descendants, his family,[NOTE:1] and his dynasty.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “his throne.”

verses.zh: 于是耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅上去，将约押杀死，葬在旷野约押自己的坟墓（原文是房屋）里。
verses.en: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and executed Joab;[NOTE:1] he was buried at his home in the wilderness.
notes: Heb “struck him and killed him.” The referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 王就立耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅作元帅，代替约押，又使祭司撒督代替亚比亚他。
verses.en: The king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada to take his place at the head of[NOTE:1] the army, and the king appointed Zadok the priest to take Abiathar’s place.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “over.”
The Old Greek translation includes after v. 35 some fourteen verses that are absent from the MT.

verses.zh: 王差遣人将示每召来，对他说：「你要在耶路撒冷建造房屋居住，不可出来往别处去。
verses.en: Next the king summoned[NOTE:1] Shimei and told him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem[NOTE:2] and live there, but you may not leave there to go anywhere.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “sent and summoned.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “and you may not go out from there here or there.”

verses.zh: 你当确实地知道，你何日出来过汲沦溪，何日必死！你的罪（原文是血）必归到自己的头上。」
verses.en: If you ever do leave and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will certainly die. You will be responsible for your own death.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your blood will be upon your head.”

verses.zh: 示每对王说：「这话甚好！我主我王怎样说，仆人必怎样行。」于是示每多日住在耶路撒冷。
verses.en: Shimei said to the king, “My master the king’s proposal is acceptable.[NOTE:1] Your servant will do as you say.”[NOTE:2] So Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Good is the word, as my master the king has spoken.”
Heb “so your servant will do.”
Heb “many days.”

verses.zh: 过了三年，示每的两个仆人逃到迦特王玛迦的儿子亚吉那里去。有人告诉示每说：「你的仆人在迦特。」
verses.en: Three years later two of Shimei’s servants ran away to King Achish son of Maacah of Gath. Shimei was told, “Look, your servants are in Gath.”

verses.zh: 示每起来，备上驴，往迦特到亚吉那里去找他的仆人，就从迦特带他仆人回来。
verses.en: So Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to find his servants; Shimei went and brought back his servants from Gath.

verses.zh: 有人告诉所罗门说：「示每出耶路撒冷往迦特去，回来了。」
verses.en: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had then returned,

verses.zh: 王就差遣人将示每召了来，对他说：「我岂不是叫你指着耶和华起誓，并且警戒你说『你当确实地知道，你哪日出来往别处去，那日必死』吗？你也对我说：『这话甚好，我必听从。』
verses.en: the king summoned[NOTE:1] Shimei and said to him, “You will recall[NOTE:2] that I made you take an oath by the Lord, and I solemnly warned you, ‘If you ever leave and go anywhere,[NOTE:3] know for sure that you will certainly die.’ You said to me, ‘The proposal is acceptable; I agree to it.’[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “sent and summoned.”
Heb “Is it not [true]…?” In the Hebrew text the statement is interrogative; the rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course it is.”
Heb “here or there.”
Heb “good is the word; I have heard.”

verses.zh: 现在你为何不遵守你指着耶和华起的誓和我所吩咐你的命令呢？」
verses.en: Why then have you broken the oath you made before the Lord and disobeyed the order I gave you?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Why have you not kept the oath [to] the Lord and the commandment I commanded you?”

verses.zh: 王又对示每说：「你向我父亲大卫所行的一切恶事，你自己心里也知道，所以耶和华必使你的罪恶归到自己的头上；
verses.en: Then the king said to Shimei, “You are well aware of the way you mistreated my father David.[NOTE:1] The Lord will punish you for what you did.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “You know all the evil, for your heart knows, which you did to David my father.”
Heb “The Lord will cause your evil to return upon your head.”

verses.zh: 惟有所罗门王必得福，并且大卫的国位必在耶和华面前坚定，直到永远。」
verses.en: But King Solomon will be empowered,[NOTE:1] and David’s dynasty[NOTE:2] will endure permanently before the Lord.”
notes: Or “blessed.”
Heb “throne.”

verses.zh: 于是王吩咐耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，他就去杀死示每。这样，便坚定了所罗门的国位。
verses.en: The king then gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada who went and executed Shimei.[NOTE:1] So Solomon took firm control of the kingdom.[NOTE:2]
notes: “The king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada and he went out and struck him down and he died.”
“And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.”
